The equation of the plane containing the triangle \(OQS\) is \(x-y=0\)
The length of the perpendicular from \(P\) to the plane containing the triangle \(OQS\) is \(\dfrac3{\sqrt2}\)
The perpendicular distance from \(O\) to the straight line containing \(RS\) is \(\sqrt{\dfrac{15}2}\)

questions.sol: Direction of the line: \((2,1,-1)\times(1,2,1)=(3,-3,3)\). The line in (b) has direction \((3,-3,3)\) too — parallel. \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{2+2-1}6=\dfrac12\). \(P_3\): \(x-y+z=0\); distance of \((2,1,1)\) is \(\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: Let \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) denote the lines \(\vec r=\hat i+\lambda(-\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k)\), \(\lambda\in R\) and \(\vec r=\mu(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)\), \(\mu\in R\) respectively. If \(L_3\) is a line which is perpendicular to both \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) and cuts both of them, then which of the following options describe(s) \(L_3\)?
opts: \(\vec r=\dfrac13(2\hat i+\hat k)+t(2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)\), \(t\in R\)
\(\vec r=\dfrac29(4\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)+t(2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)\), \(t\in R\)
\(\vec r=\dfrac29(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)+t(2\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)\), \(t\in R\)
questions.sol: Direction \((-1,2,2)\times(2,-1,2)=(6,6,-3)\). With \(A=(1-\lambda,2\lambda,2\lambda)\), \(B=(2\mu,-\mu,2\mu)\) and \(\vec{AB}\parallel(2,2,-1)\): \(\lambda=\dfrac19\), \(\mu=\dfrac29\); \(A=\dfrac29(4,1,1)\), \(B=\dfrac29(2,-1,2)\), mid point \(\dfrac13(2,0,1)\). questions.q:
Let \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) be the following straight lines.
\(L_1:\dfrac{x-1}1=\dfrac y{-1}=\dfrac{z-1}3\) and \(L_2:\dfrac{x-1}{-3}=\dfrac y{-1}=\dfrac{z-1}1\).
Suppose the straight line \(L:\dfrac{x-\alpha}l=\dfrac{y-1}m=\dfrac{z-\gamma}{-2}\) lies in the plane containing \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), and passes through the point of intersection of \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). If the line \(L\) bisects the acute angle between the lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.sol: The directions \((1,-1,3)\) and \((-3,-1,1)\) have equal length and positive dot product, so the acute bisector is along their sum \((-2,-2,4)\parallel(1,1,-2)\): \(l=m=1\). Through \((1,0,1)\): \(1-\alpha=-1=\dfrac{1-\gamma}{-2}\), so \(\alpha=2\), \(\gamma=-1\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) be real numbers such that \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\ne0\) and \(\alpha+\gamma=1\). Suppose the point \((3,2,-1)\) is the mirror image of the point \((1,0,-1)\) with respect to the plane \(\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma z=\delta\). Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.sol: Normal \(\parallel(2,2,0)\): \(\alpha=\beta\), \(\gamma=0\), so \(\alpha=\beta=1\). The mid point \((2,1,-1)\) lies on the plane: \(\delta=3\).

questions.q:
Let \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) be two planes given by
\(P_1:10x+15y+12z-60=0\),
\(P_2:-2x+5y+4z-20=0\).
Which of the following straight lines can be an edge of some tetrahedron whose two faces lie on \(P_1\) and \(P_2\)?
questions.sol: An edge must either lie in \(P_1\) or \(P_2\), or meet the two planes at two different points. (a) meets them at \(z=\dfrac{35}{12}\) and \(z=\dfrac{17}4\) ✓. (b) meets \(P_1\) at \((6,0,0)\) and \(P_2\) at \((1,2,3)\) ✓. (d) passes through \((0,4,0)\) and its direction satisfies \(-2-10+12=0\): it lies in \(P_2\) ✓. (c) is not in either plane and meets both at the same point \((0,4,0)\) ✗.

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the reflection of a point \(Q\) with respect to the plane given by \(\vec r=-(t+p)\hat i+t\hat j+(1+p)\hat k\), where \(t\) and \(p\) are real parameters and \(\hat i,\hat j,\hat k\) are the unit vectors along the three positive coordinate axes. If the position vectors of \(Q\) and \(S\) are \(10\hat i+15\hat j+20\hat k\) and \(\alpha\hat i+\beta\hat j+\gamma\hat k\) respectively, then which of the following is/are true ?

Let \(\mathbb R^3\) denote the three-dimensional space. Take two points \(P=(1,2,3)\) and \(Q=(4,2,7)\). Let \(dist(X,Y)\) denote the distance between two points \(X\) and \(Y\) in \(\mathbb R^3\). Let
\(S=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:(dist(X,P))^2-(dist(X,Q))^2=50\}\) and
\(T=\{Y\in\mathbb R^3:(dist(Y,Q))^2-(dist(Y,P))^2=50\}\).
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: There is a triangle whose area is \(1\) and all of whose vertices are from \(S\).
There are two distinct points \(L\) and \(M\) in \(T\) such that each point on the line segment \(LM\) is also in \(T\).
There are infinitely many rectangles of perimeter \(48\), two of whose vertices are from \(S\) and the other two vertices are from \(T\).
There is a square of perimeter \(48\), two of whose vertices are from \(S\) and the other two vertices are from \(T\).
questions.sol: \(S\) is the plane \(6x+8z=105\) and \(T\) the parallel plane \(6x+8z=5\), at distance \(10\). Planes contain triangles of any area and whole segments. A rectangle with one side in each plane has the other sides of length \(\ge10\); perimeter \(48\) is possible in infinitely many ways (e.g. sides \(b\ge10\), \(24-b\)), including the square of side \(12\).

questions.q: A straight line drawn from the point \(P(1,3,2)\), parallel to the line \(\dfrac{x-2}1=\dfrac{y-4}2=\dfrac{z-6}1\), intersects the plane \(L_1:x-y+3z=6\) at the point \(Q\). Another straight line which passes through \(Q\) and is perpendicular to the plane \(L_1\) intersects the plane \(L_2:2x-y+z=-4\) at the point \(R\). The perimeter of the triangle \(PQR\) is \(\sqrt2+\sqrt6+\sqrt{11}\)

questions.q: If \(A,B,C,D\) are any four points in a space; prove that \(\left|\vec{AB}\times\vec{CD}+\vec{BC}\times\vec{AD}+\vec{CA}\times\vec{BD}\right|=4\) (Area of triangle \(ABC\)).
questions.sol: Take \(D\) as origin, with \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c\) the position vectors of \(A,B,C\). The expression is \(-(\vec b-\vec a)\times\vec c-(\vec c-\vec b)\times\vec a-(\vec a-\vec c)\times\vec b=-2(\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a)\), and \(|\vec a\times\vec b+\vec b\times\vec c+\vec c\times\vec a|=2\,\)(area of \(\Delta ABC\)).

questions.q:
Find \(3\)-dimensional vectors \(\vec u_1,\vec u_2,\vec u_3\) satisfying
\(\vec u_1\cdot\vec u_1=4\), \(\vec u_1\cdot\vec u_2=-2\), \(\vec u_1\cdot\vec u_3=6\),
\(\vec u_2\cdot\vec u_2=2\), \(\vec u_2\cdot\vec u_3=-5\), \(\vec u_3\cdot\vec u_3=29\)
questions.ans: One such set: \(\vec u_1=2\hat i\), \(\vec u_2=-\hat i+\hat j\), \(\vec u_3=3\hat i-2\hat j+4\hat k\)
questions.sol: Choose \(\vec u_1=2\hat i\). Then \(\vec u_2=-\hat i+y\hat j\) with \(1+y^2=2\): take \(y=1\). \(\vec u_3=3\hat i+p\hat j+q\hat k\): \(-3+p=-5\), \(p=-2\); \(9+4+q^2=29\), \(q=\pm4\). (Any rotation of this set also works.)

questions.q: \(ABCD\) is the base of parallelopiped \(T\) and \(A'B'C'D'\) be the upper face. The parallelopiped is compressed so that the vertex \(A'\) shifts to \(A''\) on a parallelopiped \(S\). If volume of new parallelopiped \(S\) is \(90\%\) of the parallelopiped \(T\). Prove that locus of \(A''\) is a plane.
questions.sol: Volume = (area of base \(ABCD\)) \(\times\) height, and the base is unchanged. So the height of \(A''\) above the base is \(0.9\) times that of \(A'\): \(A''\) lies on a fixed plane parallel to \(ABCD\).

questions.q: Two lines having direction ratios \((1,0,-1)\) and \((1,-1,0)\) are parallel to a plane passing through \((1,1,1)\). This plane cuts co-ordinate axes at \(A,B,C\). Find volume of tetrahedron \(OABC\).
Find the equation of the plane at a distance of \(\dfrac1{\sqrt6}\) from the point \((2,1,-1)\) and containing the line \(2x-y+z-3=0=3x+y+z-5\).
The area of the triangle whose vertices are \(A(1,-1,2)\), \(B(2,1,-1)\), \(C(3,-1,2)\) is .........
The unit vector perpendicular to the plane determined by \(P(1,-1,2)\), \(Q(2,0,-1)\), \(R(0,2,1)\) is ...........

Column IColumn II
(i) Two rays in the first quadrant \(x+y=|a|\) and \(ax-y=1\) intersect each other in the interval \(a\in(a_0,\infty)\), the value of \(a_0\) is(A) \(2\)
(ii) Point \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) lies on the plane \(x+y+z=2\). Let \(\vec a=\alpha\hat i+\beta\hat j+\gamma\hat k\), \(\hat k\times(\hat k\times\vec a)=0\), then \(\gamma=\)(B) \(4/3\)
(iii) \(\left|\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-y^2)dy\right|+\left|\displaystyle\int_1^0(y^2-1)dy\right|=\)(C) \(\pi/2\)
(iv) If \(\sin A\sin B\sin C+\cos A\cos B=1\), then the value of \(C=\)(D) \(1\)
questions.sol: (i) The rays meet at \(x=\dfrac{1+|a|}{1+a}\), \(y=\dfrac{a|a|-1}{1+a}\); \(y>0\) needs \(a>1\). (ii) \(\hat k\times(\hat k\times\vec a)=\gamma\hat k-\vec a=0\) gives \(\alpha=\beta=0\), so \(\gamma=2\). (iii) \(\dfrac23+\dfrac23\). (iv) \(\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B\sin C\le\cos(A-B)\le1\), with equality only if \(\sin C=1\).

questions.q:
Column IColumn II
(i) \(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^\infty\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac1{2i^2}\right)=t\), then \(\tan t=\)(A) \(1\)
(ii) Sides \(a,b,c\) of a triangle \(ABC\) are in A.P. and \(\cos\theta_1=\dfrac a{b+c}\), \(\cos\theta_2=\dfrac b{a+c}\), \(\cos\theta_3=\dfrac c{a+b}\), then \(\tan^2\left(\dfrac{\theta_1}2\right)+\tan^2\left(\dfrac{\theta_3}2\right)=\)(B) \(2\sqrt2\)
(iii) A line is perpendicular to \(x+2y+2z=0\) and passes through \((0,1,0)\). The perpendicular distance of this line from the origin is(C) \(\dfrac{\sqrt5}3\)
(iv) A plane passes through \((1,-2,1)\) and is perpendicular to two planes \(2x-2y+z=0\) and \(x-y+2z=4\). The distance of the plane from the point \((1,2,2)\) is(D) \(2/3\)
questions.sol: (i) \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac1{2i^2}=\tan^{-1}(2i+1)-\tan^{-1}(2i-1)\); the sum telescopes to \(\dfrac\pi2-\dfrac\pi4\). (ii) \(\tan^2\dfrac\theta2=\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{1+\cos\theta}\): sum \(=\dfrac{(b+c-a)+(a+b-c)}{a+b+c}=\dfrac{2b}{3b}\). (iii) \(\dfrac{|(0,1,0)\times(1,2,2)|}3=\dfrac{\sqrt5}3\). (iv) Plane \(x+y+1=0\): \(\dfrac4{\sqrt2}\).

questions.q:
Consider the following linear equations
\(ax+by+cz=0\)
\(bx+cy+az=0\)
\(cx+ay+bz=0\)
Match the conditions/expressions in Column I with statements in Column II.
Column IColumn II
(i) \(a+b+c e0\) and \(a^2+b^2+c^2=ab+bc+ca\)(A) the equations represent planes meeting only at a single point
(ii) \(a+b+c=0\) and \(a^2+b^2+c^2 e ab+bc+ca\)(B) the equations represent the line \(x=y=z\)
(iii) \(a+b+c e0\) and \(a^2+b^2+c^2 e ab+bc+ca\)(C) the equations represent identical planes.
(iv) \(a+b+c=0\) and \(a^2+b^2+c^2=ab+bc+ca\)(D) the equations represent the whole of the three dimensional space.
questions.sol: The determinant is \(-(a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)\), and \(a^2+b^2+c^2=ab+bc+ca\) means \(a=b=c\). (i) \(a=b=c\ne0\): all three are \(x+y+z=0\). (ii) determinant \(0\) and \((1,1,1)\) is a solution: the line \(x=y=z\). (iii) determinant \(\ne0\): only the origin. (iv) \(a=b=c=0\): every point satisfies them.

questions.q: If the distance between the plane \(Ax-2y+z=d\) and the plane containing the lines \(\dfrac{x-1}2=\dfrac{y-2}3=\dfrac{z-3}4\) and \(\dfrac{x-2}3=\dfrac{y-3}4=\dfrac{z-4}5\) is \(\sqrt6\), then \(|d|\) is
questions.sol: Normal \((2,3,4)\times(3,4,5)=(-1,2,-1)\): the plane is \(x-2y+z=0\), so \(A=1\) and \(\dfrac{|d|}{\sqrt6}=\sqrt6\).

questions.q: Let \(\vec a=-\hat i-\hat k\), \(\vec b=-\hat i+\hat j\) and \(\vec c=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k\) be three given vectors. If \(\vec r\) is a vector such that \(\vec r\times\vec b=\vec c\times\vec b\) and \(\vec r\cdot\vec a=0\), then the value of \(\vec r\cdot\vec b\) is
questions.sol: \((\vec r-\vec c)\times\vec b=0\): \(\vec r=\vec c+t\vec b\). \(\vec r\cdot\vec a=-4+t=0\), \(t=4\). \(\vec r\cdot\vec b=\vec c\cdot\vec b+4|\vec b|^2=1+8\).

questions.q: Let \(P\) be a point in the first octant, whose image \(Q\) in the plane \(x+y=3\) (that is, the line segment \(PQ\) is perpendicular to the plane \(x+y=3\) and the mid-point of \(PQ\) lies in the plane \(x+y=3\)) lies on the \(z\)-axis. Let the distance of \(P\) from the \(x\)-axis be \(5\). If \(R\) is the image of \(P\) in the \(xy\)-plane, then the length of \(PR\) is _____ .
questions.sol: The image of \((a,b,c)\) in \(x+y=3\) is \((3-b,3-a,c)\); on the \(z\)-axis: \(a=b=3\). \(\sqrt{b^2+c^2}=5\) gives \(c=4\), and \(PR=2c\).
